structure: Sequential joint law with fixed parameters (one cohort, no parameter draws). (1) Sex is Bernoulli with P(F)=0.56. (2) Age is 18 + 72*Beta(1, 2.75), floored to completed years (support 18-89), independent of sex. (3) BMI given sex and age is lognormal, with a sex-specific geometric mean and log-SD and a small assumed log-linear age trend, truncated to [13, 50] kg/m^2 and rounded to 2 decimals. (4) TC and HDL in mmol/L each equal a conditional mean that is exactly linear in the requested design columns ((age-50)/10, I(sex=='F'), (bmi-25)/5) plus a mean-zero additive error. The two errors are shifted lognormals (bounded below, right-skewed), independent of covariates and coupled through a bivariate normal latent. The latent correlation is solved in code so that the Pearson correlation of the errors equals the stated residual correlation. Because the conditional means are exactly linear in the analysis design and the errors are independent of covariates, the requested OLS projections and residual correlation are closed-form functions of the model parameters. Source statistics (geometric means, quartiles, log-scale or scale-unresolved univariate slopes, Spearman correlations) only informed the parameter choices through explicit, unverified bridges; they are neither model parameters nor the requested estimands. The id prefix and width are non-scientific formatting.

requested_estimands.derivation: E[HDL | age, sex, bmi] is exactly linear in the analysis design, with mean-zero error independent of covariates and a non-singular design. The population OLS BMI coefficient times 5 therefore equals /lipids/hdl_cholesterol/mean_coefficients/bmi_per_5 = -0.03 mmol/L per 5 kg/m^2. Multiplying by the supplied numerical factor 38.67 gives -1.1601. All generated rows are eligible and no lipid truncation is active. This is a model-implied value under assumed parameters, not an estimate of the Turkana quantity.

Same argument as for HDL: the population OLS BMI coefficient times 5 equals /lipids/total_cholesterol/mean_coefficients/bmi_per_5 = 0.25 mmol/L per 5 kg/m^2, and 0.25 * 38.67 = 9.6675. This is a model-implied value under assumed parameters, not an estimate of the Turkana quantity.

The population OLS residuals equal the additive errors, because the conditional means are exactly linear in the design. For shifted lognormals built on a bivariate normal latent with correlation r, the Pearson correlation is (exp(r*sigmaT*sigmaH) - 1)/(cvT*cvH). The code solves r (about 0.365) so that this equals /lipids/residual_pearson_correlation = 0.35. The correlation is unit-free, so the mg/dL conversion does not change it.

limitations: No Turkana data, composition or outcome statistics were used. Age, sex, BMI and lipid levels are transported from Malawi, Uganda and Ghana summaries by assumption; the Turkana/Laikipia site and lifestyle mixture is unspecified and not modelled.

The three requested values are consequences of assumed parameters. The bridges behind them (unresolved log base, unresolved Greiner regression scale, Spearman-to-Pearson, univariate-to-adjusted) are unverified. Rough plausible ranges are about 8 to 19 mg/dL per 5 kg/m^2 for TC, about -2 to 0 for HDL, and about 0.1 to 0.5 for the residual correlation.
Parameter uncertainty is not propagated into the rows: one fixed-parameter cohort is generated. Source confidence intervals were treated as estimation uncertainty and never as individual dispersion.

Source lipids are mostly fasting laboratory serum assays. The target is CardioChek Plus on venous EDTA blood with fasting not established. No assay bridge, device resolution, reportable-range censoring or measurement-error component is modelled.
Source selections (exclusion of pregnancy, HIV, diabetes, prior disease; age 40-60 in Agongo) differ from the target, which applies no such exclusions. No selection correction was attempted.

Structural simplifications: linear homoscedastic conditional means, no interactions, sex independent of age, an assumed age-BMI trend, assumed age effects on lipids (the HDL age coefficient of zero is a placeholder), bounded age (18-89) and BMI (13-50) support, and a parametric shifted-lognormal error shape.
TC >= HDL is not enforced, consistent with the task's no-inferred-exclusions list; non-HDL cholesterol was not targeted.

Curator extractions were taken as supplied and not re-authenticated. Internal source discrepancies (Agongo men count, Greiner table denominators, quarantined CI) were preserved and not used for weighting.
Finite-sample OLS and correlation results from a 3000-row draw will differ from the model-implied values by sampling variability.
checks_actually_performed: Hand algebra only, during authoring: the minimum conditional lipid means on the covariate support exceed the error shifts, so the positive floor is inactive.
Hand algebra only: Beta(1, 2.75) quartiles on [18, 90]; feasibility of the latent correlation (about 0.365, within [-1, 1]); unit conversions 0.25*38.67 and -0.03*38.67.
No code was executed, no simulation was run and no data were examined.
